# Pursuit

Self-hosted job-application tracker. The CLI is the agent interface. Do not expect an MCP server.

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $PURSUIT_TOKEN` or `pursuit --token`. Scopes: read, write, approve. write does not grant approve. Nothing moves to submitting without `pursuit approve` from an approve-scoped token. A human can run `pursuit auth login` (browser, or `--device`) to store a read,write token per server; OAuth never grants approve (`invalid_scope`). `PURSUIT_TOKEN` and `--token` still win over it; without them, the CLI uses the stored login. Agents must not approve a login: approving at `/authorize` or `/device` needs a same-origin dashboard session with approve. OAuth2 endpoints: POST /v1/auth/device_authorization, POST /v1/auth/token, POST /v1/auth/revoke.

JSON: stdout is compact JSON when it is not a terminal, or with `--json`. Errors are always JSON on stderr. `--fields a,b` trims responses. `--dry-run` on mutations writes nothing. `--idempotency-key` replays a successful mutation.

Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage, 3 not found, 4 conflict, 5 auth, 6 validation, 1 other.

```
pursuit apps list --status to_apply --fields id,company,title,status
pursuit apply APP_ID --prepare
pursuit apply --batch status=to_apply --async
pursuit queue claim --worker agent-1
pursuit approve APP_ID
pursuit reject APP_ID
pursuit links
pursuit events --follow
pursuit check-links --all
pursuit schema apps update
```

OpenAPI: GET /openapi.json. One command's flags: `pursuit schema <command>`.
Auth guide for agents (tokens, scopes, approval, 401/403): GET /auth.md.
SQLite is the default database. Postgres is for more than one replica.

The browser extension uses GET /v1/profile, GET /v1/applications/by-url?url=, and POST /v1/applications/capture. It needs a write token and PURSUIT_CORS_ORIGINS. It does not approve or submit.

The dashboard at `/` is for a person. Agents keep using the CLI. `POST /v1/approvals/reject` declines `awaiting_review` work (approve scope) and does not submit. `GET /v1/links?attention=true` lists closed or changed postings. On Vercel, `GET /v1/cron/links` is the daily link check and it requires `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`. `PURSUIT_TRUST_PROXY_AUTH=vercel` is for a human behind deployment protection. Agents still send a Pursuit token.

Debugging with the audit log. Every successful change records who did what and when, with details in `metadata`.

```bash
pursuit audit list --entity-id APP_ID --sort created_at   # one application's history, oldest first
pursuit audit list --q needs_input --since 2026-10-30      # text in summary, action, entity, actor, or metadata
pursuit audit list --actor agent-1 --until 2026-10-30T12:00:00Z
```

A rejected request leaves no entry, so a missing step is the clue: compare the trace with what should have happened, then check the server log by `request_id`. The dashboard's Settings, Audit log page has "Copy for an agent", which copies the same entries as JSON with the command that reproduces them.
